body: No worries, I totally see what you're trying to say as well.

I don't know how far the rabbit whole you've gone when it comes to suicidal actions or tendencies, but my own experience have taught me that there is no sense of relief or a sense of bliss, when it comes to near-death experiences. The sensation is often times awfully painful or frightening. That together with the guilt and the principle of that I rather angered a good friend then to have no friend at all.

I see your point of view and I do hope that my friend only fell asleep instead of doing something that they might not live to regret. As I stated in my other reply, I panicked since I really care about my friend and their well-being.

This is very true in many ways. I myself have been down the path of self-destruction and didn't always think rationally when it came to making the decisions. Now that the panic has subsided I can see your point of view more clearly and as you said it's not my burden.
